scope: Theorem 22.4 (Original-data exterior rigidity) of the manuscript “Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity” (preprints/Spacetime-Penrose-inequalities-enclosing-area-charge-and-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 121. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (Ω, g, K) belong to Definition 22.3, and put m = q E2 − |P|2 δ. Then (22.6) m = 1 2  A ω 2/3 if and only if the original initial data admit a global smooth spacelike embedding, including S, into the regular maximal extension of gm. The image lies in the closure of the corresponding exterior, the chosen end approaches its spatial infinity, and S maps to a smooth section of its future horizon or to its bifurcation sphere. The pullback of the spacetime metric is g; for a consistent future unit normal n, the second fundamental form is precisely the original tensor K, with the convention (22.7) K(U, V ) = gm(∇U n, V ). Both the embedding and the normal extend smoothly to S in horizon-regular coordinates. Equivalently, every such Schwarzschild–Tangherlini hypersurface in gM0 satisfying Defini- tion 22.3 and the prescribed asymptotic hypotheses has invariant ADM mass M0, horizon area ω(2M0)3/2, and equality in Theorem 22.2.
